fact_check.claim: Bitcoin closed above the 50-week moving average for the first time in 11 months on a weekly close; two consecutive weekly closes above it make the bull market official (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified and made precise: the week ending Sept 20, 2026 closed at $81,159, above the 50-week SMA of about $78,788, the first weekly close above it since Nov 9, 2025 (45 weeks below); own recomputation from CoinGecko Sunday closes gives a 50-week SMA of about $78,740 and a Sept 20 close of $81,169, consistent. BTC $85,533 at drafting (+5.3% 24h). The two-consecutive-closes rule is Mike's own and is written as 'my rule' / 'in my book'. Copy says '45 weeks' rather than '11 months'
fact_check.source: cryptobriefing.com/bitcoin-50-week-moving-average-breakout-september-2026 (fetched 2026-09-21); tradingview.com news cryptobriefing 18b6c23cc094b; thecryptobasic.com 2026/09/21; api.coingecko.com coins/bitcoin/market_chart days=365 and simple/price (fetched 2026-09-21)

fact_check.claim: Benjamin Cowen admitted he was wrong: 'clearly I was wrong', 'I was wrong, not going to make excuses, I deserve to be dunked on' (transcript, reading his posts and video)
fact_check.verdict: verified verbatim: on Sept 21, 2026 Cowen posted 'I was wrong. Not going to make excuses. I deserve to be dunked on'. Prior call: on Sept 8 he put 65% odds on the cycle low still being ahead (35% already in), October as the potential bottom window, $53K as key support, downside scenarios toward $44K, based on 2014/2018/2022 patterns. The $85K breakout liquidated $647.9M of shorts in 24 hours ($746.6M total). Saylor replied 'welcome back' (not used). Copy quotes the three lines exactly, says 'on Sept 8 he had 65% odds on the cycle low still being ahead, with $44K in his downside scenarios' and '$648M of shorts got liquidated in a day'
fact_check.source: kucoin.com/news/flash/benjamin-cowen-admits-mistake-as-bitcoin-surpasses-85k-triggering-massive-short-liquidations (fetched 2026-09-21); benzinga.com 2026/09 michael-saylor-says-welcome-back; cryptotimes.io 2026/09/21 cowen-scrap-october-bottom-call; mitrade.com beincrypto BTCUSD-202609220948

fact_check.claim: Cowen believed in lengthening cycles back in 2020 before becoming the four-year cycle camp's figurehead (transcript: 'in 2020... he believed in the lengthening cycles theory')
fact_check.verdict: verified: during 2020 and 2021 Cowen argued for lengthening cycles with diminishing returns (vs PlanB's stock-to-flow) and declared the model dead in May 2022 after the tops kept arriving on the four-year schedule. Copy: 'back in 2020 he believed in lengthening cycles, then joined the four-year camp and became its king'. 'King of the four-year cycle zombies' is Mike's own label (persona named_opposition)

fact_check.claim: Mike's read: four-year cycle believers sold from October 2025 through March 2026 and will buy back around October; some are early because they realize the bottom is in; 'transfer of wealth', 'they're going to pump our bags' (transcript, his on-chain chart)
fact_check.verdict: Mike's own thesis, written in first person; the persona drafting rule is honored: copy never says the zombies cause an October bottom, it says they sold waiting for one, the real low printed in June, and they buy back higher than they sold

yt_posts.body_style: stat-stack-and-conclusion: the weekly close and the 50-week SMA, Galaxy's 11 of 13, Cowen's admission and his prior call, the zombies' sell-and-buy-back transfer of wealth, Mike's two-close rule, the year-five / mid-cycle-top thesis with the Bitwise quote, the black-swan caveat
yt_posts.body:
Bitcoin just did something it had not done in 45 weeks, and the king of the four-year cycle zombies posted 'I was wrong' the next day.

The weekly candle closed at $81,159 on September 20. That is above the 50-week SMA (about $78,800) for the first time since November 9, 2025. Forty-five weeks below the line, and the line is reclaimed. Bitcoin is trading around $85K as I write this.

Galaxy Research went back and checked every time Bitcoin reclaimed the 50-week after a bear-market breakdown: 13 comparable cases. In 11 of the 13, no new cycle low followed.

Then Benjamin Cowen, the king of the four-year cycle zombies, posted: 'I was wrong. Not going to make excuses. I deserve to be dunked on.' On September 8 he had 65% odds on the cycle low still being ahead of us, October as the window, $44K in the downside scenarios. Smart guy, honorable admission, and the funny part is that back in 2020 he believed in lengthening cycles before he joined the four-year camp and became its king. The cycle was the problem, not him.

Here is what the zombies did. They sold from October through March because the four-year cycle told them a new bottom was coming in October 2026. The actual low printed at $58K on June 30. Now they are waking up early, realizing the bottom may already be in, and buying back higher than they sold. That is a transfer of wealth, and it goes to the people who never left. They are going to pump our bags.

My rule: two consecutive weekly closes above the 50-week SMA and the bull market is official. One down, one to go.

And I do not think this is a four-year cycle at all. I count this as year five of the current cycle. The 2025 top never broke above the average power law the way every previous mid-cycle top did, which tells me it was a mid-cycle top, not the cycle top. Bitwise's CIO told CNBC this week the crypto winter is over and this could be the strongest and longest bull market in crypto's history. I agree: multiple all-time highs, possibly one every year, for reasons that have nothing to do with a halving.

What would it take for a new bottom now? Something catastrophically bad, a real black swan. Short of that, the zombies buying back in is the fuel.

So call it in the comments: is the bear market over, or is this the head fake the zombies say it is? And if it is over, where do the zombies finally buy back in: $90K, $100K, or higher?

Hit like and subscribe if you want the macro read that ignores the four-year cycle echo chamber.
